metadata.description: Post-core feature backlog for PhotoBlaze. These ship AFTER the core viewer is stable (roadmap Phases 0-3: window, decode-to-fit, prefetch ring, hold-to-fly). Every task obeys the prime directive (faster or perf-neutral) and the project's TDD rules: pure logic isolated and unit-tested, GPU work behind the Renderer seam, golden-image tests for visuals. Shared infrastructure is factored out so it is built once: a per-photo ViewTransform (rotation + zoom + scaling mode), a translucent HUD/overlay layer, and a central configurable action/keymap.

tasks.title: Photo rotation (r / Shift+R), non-persistent
tasks.description: Rotate the current photo 90 degrees clockwise (r) and counter-clockwise (Shift+R). Each altered photo's orientation is remembered in RAM only and discarded when the app closes.
tasks.details: DONE. Rotation quadrant lives on ViewTransform (pb-render::view) with cw/ccw stepping + UV remap + w/h swap for fit; unit-tested (4x cw = identity). Per-image overrides in an in-RAM HashMap<item, Rotation> (privacy task #2); identity drops the entry. r/Shift+R bound (Shift tracked via ModifiersChanged). Applied as a GPU transform on the quad - perf-neutral, no re-decode. NOTE: a golden-image rotation render test is deferred (geometry is unit-tested instead).
tasks.testStrategy: Pure unit tests on the rotation state machine (cw wraps 0->1->2->3->0; ccw reverses). Extend pb-render fit tests for the w/h-swapped fit recompute. Property test: four cw rotations return to the original. Golden-image test: a rotated render matches its reference within tolerance.

tasks.title: Privacy: no record of viewed photos or their metadata
tasks.description: Nothing about which photos were viewed - or their pixels/metadata - is ever written to disk. The app's existence is fine to record: installation, registry file-associations, and read-only config are all allowed (owner re-scope 2026-06-27). The line is drawn at viewing history and photo data, not at the app being installed.
tasks.details: RE-SCOPED 2026-06-27 (owner, reconfirmed): this guarantee is about CONTENT, not the app's footprint. ALLOWED: the MSI installer's registry writes (ProgID, file associations, folder verb), a Start-menu shortcut, and read-only config (Task 8). FORBIDDEN: any persistent record of what was viewed or the data behind it - no thumbnail DB/cache, no recent-files/MRU of photo paths, no temp files of decoded pixels, no logging of viewed paths. Every runtime cache - the decoded ring + ResidentRing mirror, the decode pool's in-flight buffers + pending_uploads, meta_cache, rotation overrides (Tasks 1/3), the failed set, the transient toast, and on-demand EXIF reads (Task 5) - is RAM-backed and dropped on exit (Task 6). pb-core is pure (no std::fs). DONE 2026-06-27: (1) static audit - the only fs::write/File::create in the tree are in #[cfg(test)] code + the offscreen_png example; every view/cache/decode hot path is read-only (read_dir/fs::read/fs::metadata). (2) no-trace integration test `viewing_a_folder_writes_nothing_to_disk` (pb-app) snapshots a sandbox before/after a real scan+decode+EXIF session and asserts zero files created or modified. (3) guarantee + cache inventory + boundary documented in CLAUDE.md (new 'Privacy guarantee' section). Subtask 3 (opt-in persistence flag) DEFERRED - there is no on-disk cache to gate yet; scaffold it if/when one is added.
tasks.testStrategy: Integration 'no-trace' test: run a view session pointed at a sandbox and assert (via before/after filesystem diff) that NO photo-derived files (thumbnails, caches, MRU lists, decoded-pixel temp files) are created anywhere - the installer/registry are a separate process and out of scope. Static audit: no disk-write APIs on the view/cache hot paths; all caches are RAM-backed types. Document the guarantee and its new boundary in CLAUDE.md.

tasks.title: Zoom in/out (+ / -), including below fit
tasks.description: + and - zoom the current photo about its center. Zooming out can go smaller than the screen bounds (under-fit), not just larger.
tasks.details: DONE (zoom + pan). Zoom scalar (clamped 0.05x-32x) + pan offset on ViewTransform; perf-neutral GPU transforms, reset per photo. =/+ and numpad+ zoom in, -/numpad- out; HOLD-TO-ZOOM with a time-based exponential acceleration ramp (gentle start for fine tuning, faster the longer held) applied in about_to_wait. PAN added in the same change (owner request): arrow keys pan around the photo, same accel ramp, clamped to image bounds (max_pan in pb-render::view); arrows no longer advance (space=next, backspace=prev). Tier-2 re-decode when zoomed past native is deferred (GPU-scaled for now). Zoom-about-pan-focus (vs center) is a noted refinement.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure tests on zoom math: factor stepping, clamping at bounds, center-preserving transform. Property: N zoom_in steps then N zoom_out steps returns to baseline within epsilon. Golden-image tests at representative zoom levels (incl. under-fit).

tasks.title: Scaling modes: 0 original, 8 fit (default), 9 fill
tasks.description: Number keys choose the scaling mode: 0 = pixel-for-pixel original centered on screen, 8 = fit-to-screen (default, no crop), 9 = fill the screen (crop the overflowing edges).
tasks.details:
DONE. The shared per-photo ViewTransform (pb-render::view) composes mode + rotation + zoom + pan and is unit-tested; the renderer draws from it (rotation/zoom/pan are perf-neutral GPU transforms). cover_rect/original_rect added next to fit_rect. Keys 0/8/9 bound to Original/Fit/Fill. DEVIATION from the original plan: mode is GLOBAL/sticky (set once, applies as you browse) rather than per-photo non-persistent - better UX for a flick-viewer. Fill & Original decode full-res (so Fill isn't upscale-blurry); the byte-budgeted ring bounds VRAM. A mode change bumps the geometry epoch and re-buffers neighbors.

POLISH (2026-06-27): per owner request, 0 now TOGGLES original 1:1 ↔ fit (whole photo in screen) (8=fit, 9=fill stay explicit), restoring the old fit↔original single-key flip. Also, pressing any mode key (8/9/0) always resets zoom/pan to that mode's natural framing — even when already in that mode — so a mode tap doubles as 'reset my zoom' (set_scale_mode resets unconditionally; only an actual mode change re-decodes).
tasks.testStrategy: Extend pb-render fit tests: cover() fully covers the screen and crops while preserving aspect; original() is exactly native size, centered (offsets may be negative). Property tests: Fill output covers the whole viewport; Fit output never exceeds it; Original equals native dimensions. Golden-image test per mode.

Mutually-exclusive InfoMode { Off, Basic, Full }; selecting the showing mode hides it. EXIF read on demand from RAM (privacy task #2 - nothing cached to disk). hud::render_lines does the multi-line panel; lines capped to fit screen height (scroll deferred). NOTES vs spec: panel anchored bottom-right (a tall table up the right side) rather than top-right; mtime not separately formatted (EXIF DateTimeOriginal is in the tag dump). EXIF-against-fixture and golden-image tests deferred (a no-EXIF test + the live render cover the basics).

tasks.title: Esc: immediate close, then clean teardown
tasks.description: Pressing Esc immediately closes the photo and the application, cleaning up after itself once it is no longer visible.
tasks.details: On Esc, hide/close the window FIRST for an instant perceived exit, then run teardown: drop the VRAM ring, the byte LRU, decoded buffers, rotation/zoom overrides, and any metadata - implementing the privacy guarantee (Task 2). No flush-to-disk on exit. Ordering matters: the visual close happens before the heavy frees so quitting always feels instant. Register action quit (Task 8). DONE 2026-06-27: Esc (and WindowEvent::CloseRequested) route to App::begin_exit -> (1) window.set_visible(false) so it vanishes before any heavy free; (2) clear_session_state() drops the RAM-only photo-derived caches (ResidentRing reset, pending_uploads/meta_cache/rotations/failed/current/toast cleared) - no disk flush; (3) event_loop.exit(), after which Drop frees the renderer (VRAM) + joins the decode pool while the window is already gone. No-disk-on-exit is covered by Task 2's no-trace test. Visual instant-close confirmed by boot smoke test; interactive Esc timing is owner-verified (GPU/window behavior, per project norm).
tasks.testStrategy: Integration test: teardown frees/zeroes caches and the process exits 0, creating no files (shares the no-trace assertion with Task 2). Manual/perf check: the window is gone within ~1 frame of Esc.

tasks.title: Recursive directory mode (R)
tasks.description: R toggles recursive mode: the playlist spans the current directory plus every subfolder, ordered so a folder's own photos show first, then each subfolder in order, recursively - i.e. roughly full-path order.
tasks.details: When recursive mode is on, the scan walks the whole tree and rebuilds the playlist. ORDERING (confirm with owner): directory-grouped depth-first - within a directory its own images come first (natural/numeric sort so img2 < img10), then descend into each subdirectory in natural order, recursively. This differs subtly from a pure lexicographic full-path sort (where a file 'z.jpg' would sort after a subfolder 'a/'); the grouped traversal matches the owner's 'current dir's photos first, then each subfolder'. REBUILD: the app owns the ordered path list while pb-core Playlist holds count + index, so toggling re-scans, re-sorts, rebuilds Playlist (and its precomputed shuffle for the new length), and keeps the current photo by re-finding its new index. PRIVACY (Task 2): scanning reads directory entries only - no on-disk index is written. Use walkdir; skip unreadable dirs; guard against symlink loops. KEY CONFLICT: 'R' (Shift+R) was assigned to rotate-CCW in Task 1 - recommend recursive=R and moving rotate-CCW to another default (trivial via Task 8); confirm with owner. RESOLVED 2026-06-27 (owner): the recursion toggle is Ctrl+R (NOT R), leaving R/Shift+R for rotate (Task 1); and a folder opened via picker/drag-drop/association is recursive BY DEFAULT (Task 12), so this folder-grouped ordering function is the shared one those folder opens reuse.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure unit tests on the path-ordering function over a synthetic tree: a folder's files precede its subfolders' files, folders appear in natural order, natural (numeric) sort holds within a folder. Test toggle on/off keeps the current photo (index re-found). Edge cases: empty subdirs, non-image files filtered out, unreadable dirs skipped.

tasks.title: Transient command-feedback toast (white text, dark shadow)
tasks.description: When a command is invoked, briefly flash a translucent message on screen for feedback - white text with dark shadows/outline so it stays legible over any photo.
tasks.details: A transient 'toast' overlay that appears on command invocation and fades after a short timeout (~0.8-1.2s). Reuses the HUD/text-rendering layer from Task 5. White text with a dark drop-shadow or outline for legibility over light AND dark images. Each action emits a short message - e.g. 'Rotate CW', 'Fill', 'Recursive: on', 'Zoom 150%', 'Random'. Sourced from the central action dispatch (Task 8) so any action can register a feedback string. Perf-neutral: a small text quad drawn for a few frames, fading via alpha; a new command replaces the current toast. PRIVACY (Task 2): messages are transient and never logged to disk. Pick a default anchor (e.g. bottom-center). DONE 2026-06-27 (core): bottom-center transient toast implemented. pb-render gained an INDEPENDENT toast overlay layer (set_toast + toast_quad_vertices, composited over the info panel, additive — no shader/uniform/trait change). pb-app gained a Toast (hold ~0.95s then ~0.38s linear fade, re-uploaded with alpha-scaled bitmap; ~30px pill via hud::render_panel = white text + dark outline + translucent bg, like the info panel but bigger and centered). Wired to the Ctrl+R recursion toggle ('Recursive folders: on/off'); any future command (e.g. slideshow) calls App::show_toast. Deliberately NOT shown for next/prev/zoom. Compiles, clippy -D warnings + fmt clean, tests green. DEFERRED: routing via the central action dispatch (Task 8) and a full per-action message set; manual visual check pending.

tasks.title: ICC color management (in-shader) + wide-gamut & HDR output
tasks.description: Color-manage wide-gamut sources in-shader (3x3 matrix + TRC) so Display-P3 / AdobeRGB / ProPhoto render correctly; then present wide-gamut + HDR to a capable display via an fp16 scRGB swapchain.
tasks.details:
DONE (2026-06-27), grew well beyond the original sRGB-correctness scope into full wide-gamut + HDR OUTPUT. THREE layers:

(1) IN-SHADER ICC CMS — pb_decode::color reduces a source ICC to a shader-ready ColorTransform { 3x3 source-linear->BT.709 matrix, 7-param moxcms TRC, enabled }, carried on DecodedImage::color (default sRGB passthrough). Extracted per backend: JPEG APP2 (zune icc_profile), PNG/TIFF/WebP (image-crate concrete-decoder icc_profile via load_with_icc), JXL rendered_icc, HEIC/AVIF the ISOBMFF `colr` box parsed directly in wic.rs (the MS HEIF decoder returns 0 WIC color contexts — verified) handling `prof`/`rICC` ICC and `nclx` CICP. moxcms (pure Rust, was already transitive). sRGB / ~2.2-gamma-with-sRGB-primaries detected as passthrough (bit-exact). Fixes the oversaturated Display-P3 iPhone HEICs.

(2) fp16 scRGB RENDER PATH — pb-render renders the scene to an Rgba16Float scRGB-linear intermediate (SCENE_WGSL: source->scene-linear, no gamut clamp), then a present pass -> the surface. SDR 8-bit surface: extended-Reinhard tone-map (per-image peak) + sRGB-encode. HDR fp16 surface: copy scene-linear straight through. Overlay composites into the linear intermediate so one present pass serves both.

(3) WIDE-GAMUT + HDR OUTPUT (pure wgpu, NO native D3D12 interop — a DXGI fp16 flip swapchain is always scRGB) — pb_render::display::primary_hdr() (DXGI GetDesc1) detects HDR-on; if so the surface is Rgba16Float (scRGB). HDR AVIF/HEIC (PQ/HLG) decode to fp16 scene-linear via WIC's 128bppRGBAFloat (WIC does the PQ/HLG decode for us), carried through (PixelFormat::Rgba16F). Brightness baked in the scene pass (ColorUniform.scale): SDR content x sdr_white-scale, HDR content x 1.0 (absolute scRGB). Owner-confirmed on a Display-P3/HDR/1000-nit panel: P3 visibly wider than sRGB; HDR images get real highlight headroom.

DEVIATION from the original 'assume sRGB display' plan: full wide-gamut + HDR output shipped. Open tuning (followups): real SDR-white-level via DisplayConfig (200-nit default); WIC scRGB reference-white assumption; per-output (not just primary) HDR detection. macOS port = wgpu Rgba16Float surface + EDR (deferred). Known still-SDR: Radiance HDR / OpenEXR (image-crate, not WIC); CMYK JPEG.
tasks.testStrategy: DONE: pb-decode::color unit tests (sRGB passthrough, Display-P3/AdobeRGB matrix+TRC, CICP nclx, LUT-sRGB detection, garbage->passthrough); wic.rs colr-box byte-fixture tests (prof ICC + nclx, HDR-transfer detection); common::finalize_hdr_scrgb fp16 tests; pb-render golden tests (SDR round-trip bit-exact, enabled-transform curve). Verified on the real corpus via the decode example + offscreen PNG render; on-screen wide-gamut/HDR confirmed visually by the owner (the fp16/HDR swapchain is uncapturable by GDI).

tasks.title: Windows: open photos directly (file-arg, drag-drop, picker, recursive-by-default)
tasks.description: Make PhotoBlaze open photos the way a desktop app should: double-click a photo (a file association launches it with a path), drag photos or folders onto the window, or use the file picker (O). Opening a photo shows its folder flat; opening a folder browses it recursively; Ctrl+R toggles recursion at runtime.
tasks.details: Milestone A of the Windows-integration track - behavior only, plain exe, no packaging (ADR-018/019). All entry points normalize to pb-core::open: a thin app I/O shim classifies args/drops into LaunchInput { Empty | Files | Directory } (one fs::metadata call), then the PURE pb-core::open::plan -> OpenPlan { Source::Scan{roots,recursive} | Source::Explicit(files), Cursor::First | At(path) }. Policy: single file -> scan its folder FLAT, cursor on that file; many files -> exactly those; a directory -> scan RECURSIVELY, cursor first; nothing -> empty state + picker. The fs scan + extension filter stay in the app (pb-core has no I/O); pb-core resolves the cursor index (open::resolve_cursor + Playlist::with_cursor). Add the rfd crate for the native Open dialog (O = open file(s); Shift+O = open folder). Wire winit WindowEvent::DroppedFile/HoveredFile (currently unhandled). Ctrl+R re-scans with the opposite recursion and re-finds the current photo (reuse Task 9's folder-grouped ordering). Embed an app .ico + version info via a winres/embed-resource build script so the taskbar/Explorer/association icon is real. CURRENT entry point (main.rs) only accepts a directory and read_dir's it, so a double-clicked FILE path fails today - this task fixes that. This seam makes the macOS port delivery-only (Task 15). DONE 2026-06-27: all subtasks implemented in pb-app — arg/drop/picker classification via pb_core::open, recursive-by-default folders, Ctrl+R toggle, rfd picker + bare-launch empty state, window+exe icons (build.rs/winresource + decode_bytes window icon). Compiles, clippy -D warnings clean, fmt clean, new unit tests (classify_inputs/resolve_source) green. Manual GUI verification (live drag-drop, picker, post-install double-click) still pending.
tasks.testStrategy: Pure pb-core::open tests (DONE): plan() per LaunchInput variant; resolve_cursor finds target / falls back to 0; Playlist::with_cursor clamps. App-layer: file-vs-dir classification, folders default to recursive, Ctrl+R round-trip keeps the current photo, drop of file vs folder. Manual: double-click (after Task 13 assoc), drop a photo, drop a folder, bare launch -> picker.

tasks.title: Windows packaging: signed WiX/MSI installer + file associations + GitHub CI
tasks.description: Ship an installable, code-signed MSI that registers PhotoBlaze as an 'Open with' candidate for common image types and a folder right-click verb, installs a Start-menu shortcut, and uninstalls cleanly. Built and signed in GitHub Actions.
tasks.details: Milestone B (ADR-018). WiX Toolset via cargo-wix produces the MSI from workspace metadata. The .wxs declares: a PhotoBlaze.Image ProgID, per-extension OpenWithProgids for jpg/jpeg/png/gif/webp/bmp/tiff/heic/avif/jxl (NOT RAW/SVG by default), an 'Open with PhotoBlaze' Directory\shell verb (a cheap registry key - the reason we skip MSIX), a Start-menu shortcut, the app icon, and clean uninstall. Code signing via Azure Trusted Signing (owner has an account; signtool-compatible) on the .exe and .msi removes SmartScreen without MSIX. GitHub Actions: windows runner -> cargo build --release -> cargo wix -> AzureSignTool -> upload the MSI to the tagged Release. NOTE: no app/installer can silently set the Windows default handler (SID-salted UserChoice hash); the MSI only registers a candidate, and an in-app 'Set as default' deep-links ms-settings:defaultapps (Task 14). Privacy (Task 2): installer registry writes are explicitly in-bounds; the running app still writes no viewed-photo data. DONE 2026-06-27: crates/pb-app/wix/main.wxs authored (ProgId + OpenWithProgids for jpg/jpeg/jpe/jfif/png/gif/bmp/tif/tiff/webp/heic/heif/avif/jxl + Directory and Directory\Background verbs + Start-menu shortcut + ARP icon) and cargo-wix wired via [package.metadata.wix]. MSI BUILDS GREEN locally (WiX 3.11 -> PhotoBlaze-0.1.0-x86_64.msi, only the benign ICE69 shortcut warning). .github/workflows/release.yml signs exe+msi via Azure Trusted Signing (auto-skipped if secrets absent) and attaches to the Release; ci.yml runs fmt/clippy/test. Icon assets committed under crates/pb-app/icons. Signing itself unverified here (no cert secrets); post-install double-click/association behavior needs a manual check on a real machine.

tasks.details: Milestone C (ADR-018). Set-default: a button/hotkey opens ms-settings:defaultapps (or the Default Programs UI), since Windows forbids silent default seizure. Single-instance (optional): forward a newly-opened path to the running window (named pipe / mutex) instead of spawning a second window - nicer for double-click bursts; defer if it complicates the hot path. A modern Win11 inline folder verb would need an IExplorerCommand COM handler - only pursue if the 'Show more options' legacy verb from Task 13 feels inadequate. MSIX/Store: revisit only when charging money - it buys discovery + MS-managed signing/updates but costs the cheap folder verb and adds container friction.

tasks.title: HEIC/AVIF: parallel CPU libheif decode (break the WIC serialization)
tasks.description: Route HEIC/AVIF decode to CPU libheif behind the ImageDecoder seam (A/B vs WIC) so the pool's concurrent workers actually parallelize. WIC's HEVC decoder serializes (~1.7x on 8 threads, measured), capping HEIC at ~8/s no matter the worker count; libheif (no shared GPU session) runs truly parallel -> ~8x -> prefetch full-res AHEAD of the user. Preview-first + on-land sharpen already shipped (ADR-020). Full plan, phasing, and the higher-res-preview spike: docs/heic-decode-plan.md.
tasks.details: See docs/heic-decode-plan.md. Decision: ADR-020 (CPU libheif now; NVDEC deferred — iPhone HEICs are 48-tile HEVC grids that libheif handles free). Phase 0 (OWNER, blocker): install vcpkg + cmake, `vcpkg install libheif` (libde265 + dav1d), set VCPKG_ROOT, decide static/dynamic link (dynamic -> ship DLLs in the MSI, update packaging.md). Phase 1: LibHeifDecoder (libheif-rs/libheif-sys) as an ImageDecoder for HEIC+AVIF, cargo-feature-gated, A/B vs WicDecoder; reuse common::finalize_oriented + the colr/CICP color path; preview via libheif thumbnail. Phase 2: bench concurrent throughput vs WIC over 12 & 48 MP (target >=~50/s). Phase 3 (payoff): widen request_prefetch's `upgrade_item` from displayed-only to the window (current-first) so fulls prefetch AHEAD -> sharp at scroll speed; watch VRAM budget + per-frame churn. Phase 4 (gated): NVDEC (ADR-012) only if 48 MP still lags.

tasks.details: From docs/heic-decode-plan.md 'Deferred review findings': (1) HDR HEICs bypass preview-first (HDR float branch returns before allow_preview; needs SDR-thumb->HDR-full upgrade, slot format change). (2) Fill mode decodes full-res (decode_fit returns None for Fill+Original; give Fill a cover-to-screen target). (3) Decode-pool byte budget is a soft cap (reserve-before-decode; largely moot now). (4) DecodeKind::{Preview,Full} in the pool key (defensive). (5) Sync load paths (startup/resize/mode) bypass preview-first -> ~250ms HEIC freeze. (6) No unit/property tests for the tier state machine (extract pure bits).
